name: Salvage Guild
overviewQuote: "If it sank, it's ours. If it's ours, it's for sale."
origin: Formed in the second tide-year when three rival scrapper crews agreed on one price list after a bidding war got a diver killed.
corePhilosophy: Everything below the waterline is a resource, and the dead are not owed anything but a fair cut of what they were carrying.
structureHierarchy: Rustyard Master (elected by dive-count) over six Crew Chiefs; each chief runs 8-15 divers and a winch gang.
territory: The Rustyard and the flooded lower platforms of Mid-Stacks.
goalsNearTerm: Break the Gate Syndicate's grip on the dry-dock permits; certify safe dive lanes for Level 3.
goalsLongTerm: A guild-owned deep-dive bell so nobody has to rent one from Trident.
internalTensions: Old crews hoard the good lanes; newer crews think the cut-sheet favors the Master's cousins.
iconography: A rust-red wrench crossed with a harpoon hook, painted on every winch.

relationships.why: Trident sells the rebreathers the Guild can't make.

economyResources: Winch fees, lane certification stamps, a 10% cut on every Rustyard sale.
joining: Pass a three-dive check with a Crew Chief and pay the stamp fee.

name: Trident Consortium
overviewQuote: "We don't own the sea. We own the thing that lets you breathe in it."
origin: A pre-flood diving-equipment firm that survived by buying its bankrupt competitors and converting a sunk warehouse into a factory.
corePhilosophy: Safety is a subscription. Every breath should be metered, logged and billable.
structureHierarchy: Three directors (Air, Pressure, Legal) answer to a rotating chair; floor staff are indentured by equipment debt.
territory: The Trident Works, a pressurized warehouse on the mid-levels, plus kiosks across the Terraces.
goalsNearTerm: Lock in exclusive rebreather contracts with the Seawall Authority.
goalsLongTerm: Own every air supply in the Sprawl, then price it.
internalTensions: The Air director wants to open-source the rebreather design; Legal wants him gone.
iconography: Three interlocking circles in a bubble-blue trident.

relationships.why: Supplies the Wall crews' air under a renewable exclusive.
Mercy Drop gives away what Trident sells.

economyResources: Rebreather rentals, air-fill subscriptions, pressure-suit leases, dive insurance.
joining: Apply at the Works. Equipment debt is the entrance fee.

name: Mercy Drop
origin: A clinic founded by Dr. Adaeze Ruvo after the Third Flood killed forty people in a queue for the only functioning pump.
corePhilosophy: Medicine and clean water are not for sale; everything else is negotiable.
structureHierarchy: Flat structure: a Medical Lead, shift captains, and volunteers who rotate every nine tides.
territory: The Half-Sunk Lobby clinic and four dry-room outposts.
goalsNearTerm: Stock two months of antibiotics and a working decompression chamber.
goalsLongTerm: A district-wide rescue network that answers every distress call.
internalTensions: The volunteers burn out; two captains quietly take Syndicate money for supplies.
iconography: A white drop on a blue apron, stitched by hand.

relationships.why: Undercuts their air subscriptions with free refills.
Authority needs the clinic more than it likes it.

economyResources: Donations, barter-for-care, one grudging stipend from the Authority.
joining: Show up for a shift. Skills are taught; courage is not.

name: The Watching Eye
origin: A scrap-built surveillance cooperative that began as flood-gauge readers on the Seawall and kept adding cameras.
corePhilosophy: Knowledge is the only dry ground. Whoever sees everything cannot be surprised.
structureHierarchy: A Council of Nine Lenses, each responsible for a block of sensors and a rumor-trade desk.
territory: Camera nests on rooftops from the Terraces to Gate Four.
goalsNearTerm: Map every blind spot between the Choir Shrine and the Seawall.
goalsLongTerm: A complete tide-by-tide record of the Sprawl, sold to whoever asks politely.
internalTensions: One Lens has been selling footage of her own members.
iconography: A single open eye inside a rising-water ring.

relationships.why: The Choir resents being watched and jams signals.

economyResources: Footage and rumor sales, sensor maintenance fees.
joining: Trade a secret worth more than the one you take.

name: Dockers' Union
overviewQuote: "Every crate has a name. Every name has a family."
origin: Stevedores who refused a wage cut during the Wall rebuild and won by letting a convoy sink at the pier.
corePhilosophy: The people who lift the city should vote on what it lifts.
structureHierarchy: Branch stewards elected by hoist crew; a Strike Fund overseen by a tight council.
territory: Gate Four docks, Stilt Market piers, the Flooded Platform crane yard.
goalsNearTerm: Win a hazard bonus clause for dives below the third landing.
goalsLongTerm: A union seat on the Seawall Authority board.
internalTensions: Younger stewards want to strike; older ones remember what the last strike cost.
iconography: A crossed hook and a raised fist.

relationships.why: The Syndicate breaks strikes with hired muscle.

economyResources: Dues, a strike fund, control of the cranes.
joining: Join a hoist crew; the dues are a day's pay a tide.
